issues.claim: Her work formalises a one-sided error condition for safety-critical protocol verification: the hypothesis may reject strings in the target language but must not accept strings outside it.

sources.quote: This one-sided error condition arises naturally in safety-critical protocol verification.
We study the sample complexity of passive learning of regular languages in the PAC framework where learners are permitted only false-negative errors

issues.explanation: The paper studies sample complexity under an existing one-sided-error condition and notes it arises naturally in safety-critical verification; it does not 'formalise' that condition. Reword to say her work derives sample-complexity bounds for the one-sided-error learning setting motivated by safety-critical verification.
